span.label: mechanisms
span.term: OUTPUT CANNOT EXCEED INPUT: a conclusion inherits the reliability and the non-neutrality of the data it was computed from, so an algorithm cannot repair evidence that was misguided before it arrived
span.note: status: the informal ‘garbage in, garbage out’ principle clearly illustrates
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A LEARNING ALGORITHM REWRITES ITS OWN DECISION STRUCTURE WHILE RUNNING, so the rationale for any particular classification is not fixed at design time and cannot be read off the program
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: ONCE TRAINED, CLASSIFICATION PROCEEDS WITHOUT AN OPERATOR - the structure produced by training is what new inputs meet, which is why oversight has no natural point of entry
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: POPULATION KNOWLEDGE APPLIED TO AN INDIVIDUAL: correlations hold of groups while the action lands on a person, and even population-level action spills over - an insurance premium set for a sub-population is paid by each member
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: VALUES ENTER THROUGH PARAMETERS: developers specify and users configure operational parameters with desired outcomes in mind, so the algorithm privileges some interests before it processes anything
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: SECRECY IS COMMERCIALLY MOTIVATED, NOT INCIDENTAL: disclosure would enable gaming and threaten viability, so inaccessibility is a position taken in a conflict of interests rather than a technical limit
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: CORRELATIONS ARE ACTED ON WITHOUT CAUSAL KNOWLEDGE because a sufficient volume of data is treated as credible enough to drive action - the paper's name for that lowered bar is `actionable insights`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the review covers only literature that discusses algorithms explicitly, so neighbouring fields - AI ethics, surveillance studies, computer ethics, machine ethics - are touched on only briefly
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the authors accept there may be gaps in coverage for topics discussed only in relation to specific algorithm types rather than to algorithms as such
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: summarising every field in which algorithms are used is stated to be beyond reach, and the narrowing is justified on that ground
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: discussion of 'algorithm' runs into a level-of-abstraction problem: without fixing the level, parties talk past each other and the set of relevant observables is never bounded
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the authors state that a mature ethics of algorithms does not yet exist, and attribute that partly to the breadth of the concept itself
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: configuration is excluded from changing the object: tuning an algorithm to a task is said not to alter its mathematical representation or its implementation, which bounds what the map is about
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: algorithms that automate mundane tasks are excluded by declaration rather than by a criterion, and the class of interest is given without a precise definition
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the paper marks its own normative judgements as observer-dependent rather than claiming a standard: whether evidence counts as misguided, and whether an outcome counts as unfair, are both said to depend on who is evaluating
span.note: eliminates: a reader taking the map's normative labels as the authors' own ethical standard - `misguided` and `unfair` are marked observer-dependent, so the framework cannot be read as smuggling in a particular ethics · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the map is declared not to derive from any particular ethical theory, which is what lets readers who disagree about ethics still use it
span.note: eliminates: the objection that the map only works for readers who already share the authors' ethical theory - it is declared to derive from none · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: algorithm - THE PAPER HOLDS TWO SENSES AT ONCE AND SAYS SO. The formal sense is Hill's mathematical construct; the sense it actually maps is the public-discourse one, which includes the implementation into a technology and the configuration of that technology to a task. Its own point is that a map of the ethics cannot use the formal sense alone
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: algorithm - AND THE CONFLATION IS NAMED AS THE OBSTACLE, not glossed over: the same word carries a mathematical construct and 'any procedure or decision process, however ill-defined', and the paper says the mapping exercise must address that before it can begin
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: transparency - NOT ONE PROPERTY BUT TWO CONDITIONS THAT COME APART: information can be accessible and still not comprehensible, which is exactly the case machine learning creates
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: fairness - EXPLICITLY OBSERVER-DEPENDENT HERE, a generic label for whatever ethical criteria an observer brings to the action rather than a standard the paper supplies
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: inconclusive evidence - THE PAPER'S OWN CATEGORY, defined as the uncertainty that is inherent rather than accidental: inferential and machine-learning methods yield knowledge that is probable and inevitably uncertain, so the deficiency cannot be engineered away
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: inscrutable evidence - defined by a REASONABLE EXPECTATION THAT IS NOT MET: the link between data and conclusion ought to be intelligible and open to scrutiny, and given how algorithms operate that is not automatically satisfied
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: misguided evidence - defined from a limit shared by ALL data processing rather than anything specific to algorithms: the output can never exceed the input
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: transformative effects - the category for harms with NO IDENTIFIABLE VICTIM AND NO OBVIOUS FAILURE: effects that look ethically neutral because nothing was broken, yet change how the world is conceptualised and organised
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
